brief: UBS argues that rising rates (the Fed's first hike since 2023, ECB signaling more tightening, BoE flagging energy-driven inflation risk, BoJ entering a new policy phase) do not by themselves derail equities, because growth and earnings remain resilient. It likens the current setup to the constructive 2016-2017 tech cycle rather than 2022's disruption: Nasdaq 100 earnings are forecast to grow 43% this year and 28% next, cloud revenue is accelerating, and AI capex is expected to reach USD 1.2tr in 2027, so UBS favors quality semiconductor and hardware leaders. That AI buildout also extends to a bullish case on power infrastructure (gas, renewables, nuclear, storage, on-site generation) to meet data-center demand. Separately, UBS calls the recent drug-trial setback and medical-device selloff overdone, keeping a positive Longevity view. On oil, despite improving Hormuz flows, UBS sees price risk skewed higher on Houthi and Iran-US tensions and favors copper within commodities. It keeps German and Eurozone equities rated Attractive despite the AfD's regional election gains over Merz's CDU.
